To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the expression of a gene is determined by the expression level of its upstream genes, which are called regulators, (ii) the expression level of each regulator is determined by the level of its upstream regulators, (iii) the expression level and the regulation strength of a gene can be predicted from the sequence and structure of the gene, and (iv) the expression level can be predicted from its regulators and the expression level and regulation strength of the regulators.

(1) a new class of algorithms, called the "generalized linear models," is a powerful tool for modeling gene expression and regulation networks; (2) a novel method of "network component analysis" is a powerful tool to infer gene regulation networks from gene expression data.

(1) The genome-wide expression and regulation networks of the yeast and E.coli can be reconstructed from a large amount of gene expression data and protein-DNA interaction data, respectively; (2) The genome-wide networks of the yeast are more robust and more efficient than those of E.coli, which can explain why the yeast is much more resistant to the environment changes than the E.coli; (3) We have developed a new method to identify the functional modules from a network.
